Difference in differences for treatments that switch on and off

Source: R/policy_evaluation.R
swtdid.Rd

De Chaisemartin and D'Haultfoeuille's estimator of the effect at the moment units switch: in every period, units that switch into treatment are compared with units untreated in both periods, and units that switch out with units treated in both; with the placebo that runs the same comparison one period earlier.

Usage

swtdid(
  data,
  unit,
  time,
  y,
  trtd,
  cl = NULL,
  reps = 499L,
  seed = NULL,
  conflvl = 0.95
)

Arguments

data

A data frame, one row per unit and period.

unit, time, y

Column names: the unit, the period (numeric, for example a year or a month index) and the outcome.

trtd

Column name of the treatment indicator (0 or 1).

cl

Column name of the clusters (default the unit), or two column names for two-way clustering (Cameron, Gelbach and Miller 2011): \(V_a + V_b - V_{ab}\), each term with the small-sample factor of the dimension with fewer clusters, and t on its \(G - 1\) degrees of freedom. A composite cluster (district by month, say) is one column made with interaction().

reps

Bootstrap replications (default 499; 0 for none).

seed

Optional seed for the bootstrap.

conflvl

Confidence level (default 0.95).

Value

A data frame of class rmbl_switching_did, two rows (effect, placebo): estimate, se, lower, upper, switchers.

Details

For each period \(t\) with joiners (\(D_{t-1} = 0, D_t = 1\)) and stayers untreated in both, \(DID_{+,t}\) is the joiners' mean change in the outcome minus the stayers'; with leavers (1 to 0) and stayers treated in both, \(DID_{-,t}\) is the stayers' change minus the leavers'. The estimate is $$DID_M = \sum_t \frac{N_{J,t}}{N_S} DID_{+,t} + \frac{N_{L,t}}{N_S} DID_{-,t},$$ over the \(N_S\) switchers. The placebo compares, between \(t - 2\) and \(t - 1\), the change of the units that switch at \(t\) with that of the units whose treatment did not change over \(t - 2\) to \(t\); it should be near zero. Standard errors come from the cluster bootstrap. Unlike the two-way estimator, \(DID_M\) never uses a unit whose treatment changed as a control in the period it changed.

References

de Chaisemartin C, D'Haultfoeuille X (2020). Two-way fixed effects estimators with heterogeneous treatment effects. American Economic Review 110(9):2964-2996. doi:10.1257/aer.20181169

Applied as a placebo check on ward redistricting: Ternullo S, Zorro-Medina A, Vargas R (2024). How political dynasties concentrate advantage within cities. Social Forces 102(4):1310-1331. doi:10.1093/sf/soae029

Examples

p <- polex()
swtdid(p, "district", "month", "crmrate", "reformed", reps = 99, seed = 1)
#>      term   estimate        se     lower      upper switchers
#> 1  effect -3.1355000 0.4555572 -4.028376 -2.2426243        15
#> 2 placebo -0.5169222 0.4429911 -1.385169  0.3513245        15
